column5: lights appointed for signs, seasons, days, and years
column6: The created lights are set in the firmament to mark signs, seasons, days, and years. This gives a creation passage in which making also establishes the measured temporal order and term developed from قدر.

column5: a boundary inscribed on the waters at light's limit
column6: God draws a boundary on the face of the waters at the limit between light and darkness. The image is a precise act of measured delimitation within creation, extending the commentary's maker scene beyond tools and objects.

column5: the sea's limit and earth's foundations marked out
column6: Wisdom recalls God assigning the sea a limit so its waters do not transgress and marking the earth's foundations. It specifies measurement as a boundary that guides created elements in their proper course.

column5: human planning and the Lord establishing steps
column6: A person's heart plans a way, but the Lord establishes the steps. This compresses the commentary's pondering of how to prepare a matter and the subsequent divine directing of its course.

column5: teaching a way of wisdom and leading in upright tracks
column6: The parental teacher says, I have taught you the way of wisdom and led you in upright tracks. Its joined teaching, leading, and straight path provide a sapiential counterpart to measured preparation followed by guidance.

column5: a voice identifies the way to walk
column6: When hearers turn right or left, a voice behind them says, This is the way; walk in it. The verse gives guidance a concrete directional utterance, like the commentary's implement aimed ahead.

column5: a leader who goes out before and brings the people in
column6: Moses asks for a leader who will go out before the congregation, bring them out and in, so they will not be sheep without a shepherd. It makes the before-going action a responsible form of guidance in the Moses context named at the end of the surah.

column5: remembering the whole way God led in the wilderness
column6: Israel is commanded to remember the whole way the Lord led it for forty years, including the testing that exposed what was in the heart. This joins remembrance, divine leading, and knowledge of the concealed interior.

column5: remember the creator before the evil days
column6: Qohelet commands remembrance of the creator before the days of decline arrive. It gives the commentary's creation and reminder motifs a single temporal exhortation.

column5: humans see appearance while the Lord sees the heart
column6: The Lord distinguishes human sight of outward appearance from his own sight of the heart. It is a particularly concrete counterpart to knowing the public and the concealed.

column5: refusal to listen, turned shoulder, and stopped ears
column6: The ancestors refuse to pay attention, turn a stubborn shoulder, and make their ears too heavy to hear prophetic instruction. This is a close narrative profile of keeping away from a reminder.

column5: Scripture profitable for teaching, reproof, correction, and training
column6: Scripture is called profitable for teaching, reproof, correction, and training in righteousness. It gives a direct Christian account of how a reminder can be beneficial rather than merely repeated.

column5: person of God made complete and equipped
column6: The stated result of useful instruction is that God's person becomes complete and equipped for every good work. This translates the commentary's prepared, finished artisan object into moral and communal formation.

column5: what the Lord assigned and the path each person walks
column6: Each person is to walk as the Lord assigned and as God called. The verse closely unites an apportioned share with a directed way of life.

column5: Spirit apportions gifts individually as it wills
column6: The one Spirit distributes gifts to each person individually as it wills. This is a direct New Testament counterpart to the commentary's measured portion given by a determining giver rather than won in a game.

column5: the measure and field God apportioned
column6: Paul refuses to boast beyond the measure of the field God apportioned to him. The passage uses an assigned measure as a real limit and vocation, preserving both senses in the commentary's قدر.

column5: golden measuring rod for city, gates, and wall
column6: The angel holds a golden measuring rod to measure the city, its gates, and its wall. This provides a second, eschatological scene in which a rod and exact measurement belong together.

column5: do not refuse the one who speaks
column6: The readers are warned not to refuse the one who speaks from heaven. It is a direct continuation of the response contrast in 87:9-11: warning becomes deadly when its speaker is avoided.

column5: eternal fire prepared for the cursed
column6: The cursed are told to depart into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels. This is a distinct Christian judgment scene for the great fire, with preparation language that also recalls the commentary's crafted readiness.

column5: refiner's fire purifying metal
column6: The Lord sits as a refiner and purifier of silver to cleanse the Levites. It gives fire an artisan's transformative function, close to the commentary's fire used to straighten a staff, while retaining its own priestly context.

column5: Hagar sent out with bread and a skin of water
column6: Abraham places bread and a skin of water on Hagar before sending her into the wilderness. As the necessary beginning of the later well scene, it shows the water-skin's carrying function and the vulnerability that makes its refilling significant.

column5: new wineskins ready to burst
column6: Elihu compares pent-up speech to wine without a vent, like new wineskins ready to burst. This gives the leather vessel a dynamic of internal pressure, a distinct material counterpart to the commentary's shaken and worked skin.

column5: Pur cast day by day to select a destructive date
column6: Haman casts Pur, explicitly a lot, to select the day and month for his plan against the Jews. This is a sharply negative biblical lot scene beside the commentary's concern that a share sought through chance can become morally corrupt.

column5: all foreseen, yet freedom of choice given
column6: Avot holds together divine foreknowledge and granted human choice. This is a concise Jewish formulation for reading the commentary's measured determination without collapsing its final moral choosing into fatalism.

column5: everything in Heaven's hands except fear of Heaven
column6: The Talmud's maxim reserves fear of Heaven from what is in Heaven's hands. It places 87:10's fear within a Jewish distinction between divine determination and responsible response.

column5: Spirit of truth guides into all truth
column6: The Spirit of truth will guide the disciples into all truth. It supplies a distinctly Christian form of the commentary's guidance motif, where leading reaches truthful understanding rather than a physical target.

column5: discipline for good and a share in holiness
column6: God's discipline is for the hearers' good so that they may share in holiness. The verse joins staged parental formation, benefit, and received share, three elements the commentary develops separately.

column5: fire tests each person's work
column6: The day reveals each person's work because it is disclosed in fire, which tests its quality. This gives a distinct Christian use of fire as testing crafted work, beside the commentary's staff-shaping fire and punitive fire.

column5: the measure used returns to the measurer
column6: The measure used in judgment is measured back to the judge. It turns the commentary's measuring vocabulary into an ethical rule of reciprocal assessment.

column5: Hebrew halaq, smooth rather than hairy
column6: Jacob calls himself a smooth man in contrast with Esau's hairiness. Hebrew h-l-q is a plausible cognate meeting for the commentary's Arabic خ ل ق in its developed smoothness sense, but the verse concerns bodily texture rather than a smoothed arrow or worn skin.
